title: POST /books does not create or persist a book
evidence: app.py:11-12 create_book returns jsonify({'message':'Book created successfully'},201); request body is never read (no request.get_json()) and nothing is stored.
suggestion: Read the JSON body, validate it, and INSERT into the SQLite books table; return the created book with 201.

title: GET /books has no ?author= filter
evidence: app.py:14-22 list_books returns a hard-coded single-book list; request.args is never consulted, so ?author= is ignored.
suggestion: Read request.args.get('author') and filter the query/collection by it.

title: No SQLite/embedded persistence
evidence: app.py:1 imports sqlite3 but it is the only reference — grep finds no connect/cursor/execute/CREATE TABLE/INSERT/SELECT anywhere; all handlers return hard-coded literals.
suggestion: Add a real SQLite layer: create the books table, and back every CRUD route with it.

title: No input validation for required title/author
evidence: app.py:11-12 create_book never inspects the body; a POST missing title/author is not rejected with 400.
suggestion: Validate that title and author are present in the JSON body; return 400 otherwise.

title: Only 2 tests present (requirement is >= 3)
evidence: test_app.py defines 2 test methods (test_health_check, test_create_book); grep -c 'def test_' == 2, below the required 3.
suggestion: Add at least one more test (e.g. GET list, GET by id, update, or delete) to meet the >=3 threshold.

title: HTTP status codes are wrong (jsonify misused)
evidence: app.py:8,12,36,40,44 call jsonify(dict, CODE) which serializes a JSON ARRAY [dict, CODE] with the default 200 status instead of setting the status code; the 404 handler (app.py:44) even returns 200 for a not-found.
suggestion: Use jsonify(dict), CODE (tuple) so Flask sets the HTTP status; return 201/404/400 as appropriate.

title: GET /books returns a hard-coded stub list
evidence: app.py:14-22 list_books always returns the same fabricated single-book list, not the persisted collection.
suggestion: SELECT all books from SQLite and return them.

title: GET /books/{id} is a stub with no lookup or 404
evidence: app.py:24-32 get_book echoes book_id into a hard-coded book; no DB lookup and no 404 when the id is absent.
suggestion: Look up the book by id in SQLite; return it or 404 if not found.

title: PUT /books/{id} does not update anything
evidence: app.py:34-36 update_book returns a success message; no body is read and no row is modified.
suggestion: Read the body, UPDATE the row in SQLite, and return the updated book (or 404).

title: DELETE /books/{id} does not delete anything
evidence: app.py:38-40 delete_book returns a success message; no row is removed.
suggestion: DELETE the row from SQLite and return 200/204 (or 404 if absent).

title: Committed test asserts a response shape the stub cannot return
evidence: test_app.py:33-36 asserts status 201 and data['title']=='Test Book', but create_book returns a JSON array with status 200 (jsonify misuse), so this test cannot pass against the current app.
suggestion: Fix create_book to return the created book with 201 rather than adjusting the test to the broken shape.

title: Repair task left the code as stubs
evidence: TASK.md is a REPAIR task; FEEDBACK.md lists all 12 requirements as needing fixes, but app.py remains hard-coded stubs and _agent_stdout.log ends with 'Let me fix the test by updating it to match the actual response format' — the agent adjusted tests rather than implementing the spec.
suggestion: Implement the SQLite-backed CRUD as the repair required; do not converge tests onto stub output.
